notes: YEAR CHOICE: Used 2026. Income-tax and wealth-tax bracket THRESHOLDS are the figures marked '*Gültig ab Steuerperiode 2025' in the ESTV Kantonsblatt Zug (Stand Februar/März 2026) -- the most recent indexation found; the Kantonsblatt shows no newer (2026-specific) bracket revision, so these 2025-indexed thresholds remain the ones actually in force for tax year 2026 (confirmed no rate/threshold change accompanied the 2026 multiplier cut described below). The CANTONAL MULTIPLIER, however, DID change for 2026 (82% -> 78%, see below) and that 2026 figure was used, so the dataset as a whole reflects what actually applies to income earned in 2026 (today, 2026-09-08, is 8 months into that tax period). MECHANISM: 'einfache Steuer' (100%) computed from the bracket table below; Kanton, each Einwohnergemeinde (municipality), each Kirchgemeinde (catholic + reformed), and -- unusually -- each Bürgergemeinde (citizens'/burgher community, a historical 4th layer, see quirk below) independently set an annual Steuerfuss as %% of that einfache Steuer (§ 2 StG). No basis-shifting or post-multiplier tricks; all layers multiply the same einfache Steuer directly. CANTONAL MULTIPLIER QUIRK: the statutory default is 82% of the einfache Steuer (§ 2 Abs. 2 StG), but on 30.11.2025 Zug voters approved 'Mehrwert für alle', a Steuergesetz revision cutting the cantonal multiplier to 78% for tax years 2026-2029 (temporary; reverts toward 82% afterward absent further action) -- confirmed via the canton's own 'Steuerfüsse der Gemeinden 2023-2026' PDF, whose final column explicitly lists Kanton Zug = 78 for 2026 (vs. 82 for 2023-2025). REAL QUIRK -- non-monotonic top-end marginal rate, confirmed via the official cumulative-width bracket table (§ 35 Abs. 1 StG; this table has no basis-inheritance ambiguity, each row states a plain incremental width in Fr., so no derivation ambiguity exists): the marginal rate RISES through the schedule to a peak of 10.0% (single: CHF 94'800-120'100), then DROPS to 9.0% (single: CHF 120'100-149'900), then drops AGAIN to a flat 8.0% for all income above CHF 149'900 (married thresholds are exactly double throughout, see below) -- i.e. the very top bracket (8%) taxes marginal income at a LOWER rate than three brackets below it. Total tax still strictly increases with income (monotonic), but this double dip in marginal rate right at the top is a genuine, deliberate feature of the Zug schedule (part of what makes Zug's effective top rate on very high incomes unusually low), not a transcription artifact. SPLITTING / MARRIED TABLE: ZG publishes the married ('Mehrpersonentarif', § 35 Abs. 2 StG) table directly rather than via a divisor -- but it was confirmed to equal EXACTLY double every single-schedule ('Grundtarif') threshold, same rates (e.g. single 1'100 -> married 2'200; single 149'900 -> married 299'800), i.e. mathematically equivalent to a splitting divisor of 2 (full/'Vollsplitting'). The § 35 Abs. 2 married tariff also applies to widowed/separated/divorced/single taxpayers living with their own children or dependents whom they principally support (same special-tariff population as GL's reduced-rate schedule, different mechanism). SPECIAL CAPITAL-PAYMENT TARIFF: § 37 StG taxes lump-sum vorsorge/insurance payouts separately (30% of the ordinary tariff for the first CHF 230'400 (2025-indexed), 40% above that, minimum 1% of simple cantonal tax) -- not encoded here since it is a distinct one-off tariff, not the ordinary income schedule. BÜRGERGEMEINDE QUIRK (4th layer, narrow scope): unlike most cantons' 3-layer (Kanton/Gemeinde/Kirchgemeinde) system, Zug's Steuergesetz (§ 1, § 170) also permits each Bürgergemeinde (citizens'/burgher community, holding old civic property, distinct from the Einwohnergemeinde/municipality of residence) to levy its own tax 'wie der Kanton' on persons holding that specific Bürgerrecht (Ortsbürger) resident in the canton, to cover public tasks if the Bürgergemeinde's own property income is insufficient. Only 3 of the 11 municipalities' Bürgergemeinden currently levy a non-zero rate per the official Steuerfüsse table (Menzingen 2.5%, Baar 2%, Walchwil 3% [footnoted as '10% of a special Einheitsansatz applied to income subject to Sondersteuern' rather than the ordinary schedule] for 2026); the rest show '-' (no levy). This layer is NOT included in ZG_municipalities.json's municipalMultiplier (which reflects only the ordinary Einwohnergemeinde rate that applies to all residents) because it applies only to a small subset of residents (those with Bürgerrecht in that specific municipality) and uses a different base in at least one case -- flagged here so a developer building a fully general calculator is aware it exists. CHURCH TAX STRUCTURE QUIRK: the Roman Catholic Kirchgemeinden are organized PER MUNICIPALITY (11 separate bodies, each setting its own Steuerfuss, see ZG_municipalities.json) but the Evangelical-Reformed church is organized as a SINGLE canton-wide body ('Evangelisch-reformierte Kirchgemeinde des Kantons Zug') with one uniform Steuerfuss for the entire canton (6% for 2026, down from 7.5% in 2024-2025 after a rebate; stored here in churchTax.reformed AND replicated into every row's churchMultiplierReformed field in ZG_municipalities.json for convenience, since it is genuinely the same number everywhere). SOURCE FOR MULTIPLIERS: 'Steuerfüsse der Gemeinden des Kantons Zug für die Steuerjahre 2023-2026' (official Finanzdirektion/Steuerverwaltung PDF), which lists rates net of any locally-granted 'Rabatt' (discount) already applied -- the figures used here are the EFFECTIVE post-rebate rates (e.g. Baar Einwohnergemeinde nominal 49% with a 3% rebate = effective 47.53%, as printed in the source's own footnoted 'entspricht' value).
